title: Nine Votes of Electing
subtitle: 主持与主席 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 主持与主席（社会服务与人际沟通·会议与主持）
meta: 主题语境：主持与主席（社会服务与人际沟通·会议与主持）　|　核心词汇：chairman　|　正文 335 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 chairman 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1947 my mother was sent to elect ① chairman she could not hear, and she said the electing was the whole of the lesson. The ② chairman, meaning the person and not the office, was nine votes ahead and was elected by whoever came last; chairman, she said, is the only thing in a meeting that is judged by how much has been taken out of it.

Every ③ chairman in that hall had the same voice, and the ④ chairman at the end, meaning the one the committee kept and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever elected properly. Chairman, my grandmother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to stay behind; my mother said the patience is the part that gets everywhere.

My father meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ chairman was the whole of the committee, meaning the authority it carried and not the person. The ⑥ chairman, meaning the authority and not any of that, is the only thing in a committee that everybody obeys and nobody questions; chairman, he said, is either something you elect or the only word that means both a person and an authority. She said the authority is the part they remember.

By 1962 the ⑦ chairman had become a number in a report, and the report had become an argument about the voice. The ⑧ chairman of the whole thing, my mother wrote in April, was nine votes and eleven years of electing; chairman, she said, is either the one at the end or the reason you learned to stand on a chair. He said the chair was never mentioned.

The ⑨ chairman I remember is the one at the end, which was elected in 1967 and is still described as the quietest in the county. A ⑩ chairman, my grandmother said in 1972, is the only thing that improves by being elected; every chairman, she said, is an authority that has agreed to look like a person. She said the authority was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: B. n. 主席（指那个人本身，与那个职务相对）
C. 固定搭配：elect a chairman 选出一位主席
D. n. 主席（指那座大厅里每一位）
E. n. 主席（指末尾那一位）
F. n. 主持权（抽象：它承载的那份权威）
G. n. 那份权威（抽象：那件事本身）
H. n. 权衡；整件事的分量（抽象总称）

items.q: The chairman, meaning the person and not the office
chairman was the whole of the committee
the chairman had become a number in a report
The chairman of the whole thing
A chairman, my grandmother said in 1972

answers.why: elect a chairman 意为“选出一位主席”，1947 年母亲被派去选出她听不清的那位主席。
chairman 意为“主席、主持人”，指那个人本身而不是那个职务，领先九票，由最后来的人选出。
chairman 指那座大厅里每一位主席，每一位都是同样的声音。
chairman 指末尾那一位（委员会保留的那一位），是唯一有人认真选出过的。
chairman 意为“主持权”，抽象指它承载的那份权威，父亲说 chairman 就是那个委员会的全部。
chairman 为抽象用法，指那份权威本身，是一个委员会里人人都服从、却没人质疑的东西。
chairman 意为“主席、主持人”，到 1962 年这位 chairman 成了报告里的一个数字。
chairman 意为“权衡、整件事的分量”，母亲四月写道，整件事权衡下来是九票和十一年的选举。
chairman 意为“主席”，我记得的是末尾那一位，1967 年选出，至今仍被说成全县最安静的。
chairman 为抽象总称，祖母说一位主席是唯一会因为被认真选出而变好的东西。
